dct_description_sm: The project was designed to test models of glacioisostacy and to determine rates of recent marine submergence and coastal transgression.  Sediment cores were obtained with the intention of determining how inundated basins and sills change during a transgression (period of sea level rise) leading to a saltwater intrusion into formally freshwater coastal lakes. Cores along the shallow sills are used to determine how the sill changes through time as well as determining a specific height at which sea level overtopped the lowest section.  Cores in the deepest sections of the basins are used to determine the period in which the basins changed from freshwater to marine.  The transition is determined using the change in diatom composition while the period is determined through radiocarbon dating of organics found near the interface.  Together these will help constrain a local sea level curve.
dct_title_s: Sediment cores from shallow marine coastal basins, Sachs Harbour, Banks Island, NWT
